title: The Danites Move North

named.name: Zorah
named.label: below
named.note: The Danites sent five spies from Zorah and Eshtaol, and six hundred armed men set out from there (18:2, 11). The tribe had not been able to hold its allotment in the Shephelah against the Amorites (1:34).

named.name: Eshtaol
named.label: left
named.note: With Zorah, the home of the Danites (18:2, 8, 11).

named.name: Mahaneh-dan
named.label: right
named.note: The six hundred camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah, "which is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day" (18:12).

named.name: Kiriath-jearim
named.label: right
named.note: The Danites camped west of it (18:12). The ark later stayed here twenty years (1 Samuel 7:1–2).

named.name: Dan
named.label: right
named.site: Tel Dan, by the springs of the Jordan
named.note: Laish was a quiet and secure town "far from Sidon," with no ally. The Danites burned it, rebuilt it and named it Dan, and set up Micah's carved image with Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, as priest (18:7–31). Tel Dan still has a great Middle Bronze Age gate of mudbrick from the city's Canaanite days.

named.name: Beth-rehob
named.label: left
named.site: unknown; in the valley north of Laish
named.note: Laish lay "in a valley near Beth-rehob" (18:28), the upper Jordan and Hula valley running north toward the Beqaa.

named.name: Shiloh
named.label: left
named.note: Micah's image stood at Dan "all the time the house of God was in Shiloh" (18:31).

moves.text: Five Danite spies go north by way of Micah's house to Laish, and report back
Six hundred Danites camp at Mahaneh-dan, take Micah's image and priest, and fall on Laish

symbols.key: Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim (site unknown): the Danites take his carved image, ephod and priest
The six hundred camp at Mahaneh-dan
The Danites strike Laish and burn the city; they rebuild it and name it Dan

p: The last chapters of Judges are not in time order; they show what Israel had become. Twice the narrator says, "In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (17:6; 21:25). A Levite descended from Moses serves a household idol for pay, and a tribe gives up its allotment to take a peaceful town far from help. The priest is Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses (18:30), so these events took place within a few generations of the conquest.

notes.h: From the coast to the springs of the Jordan
p: Dan's allotment lay in the Shephelah and on the coast (Joshua 19:40–46), but the Amorites, and later the Philistines, pressed them into the hills (1:34). About 150 km north, Laish sat by one of the great springs of the Jordan, well watered and open. From then on Dan was Israel's northern end, "from Dan to Beersheba" (20:1), and later Jeroboam set a golden calf there (1 Kings 12:29).
